1 زَكَمَ , (K,) inf. n. زَكْمٌ, (TA,) He filled a water-skin: (K, TA:) and زَكْبٌ signifies the same as زَكْمٌ, i. e. the act of filling: this is the primary meaning. (TA.) ―
-b2- See also 4. ―
-b3- زَكَمَ بِنُطْفَتِهِ (tropical:) He emitted his sperma genitale (M, A, K) like the discharge of mucus from the nose of the مَزْكُوم. (A.) ―
-b4- زَكَمَتْ بِهِ أُمُّهُ (assumed tropical:) His mother brought him forth [in an absolute sense (as in a saying here following), or], accord. to IAar, easily. (TA.) One says, لَعَنَ ٱللّٰهُ أُمًّا زَكَمَتْ بِهِ (assumed tropical:) [May God curse a mother that brought him forth]. (TA.) ＝
-A2- زُكِمَ He (a man, S) was, or became, affected with زُكَام: (S, Msb, K:) [it is app. from زَكَمَهُ; but is thought to be] from أَزْكَمَهُ, q. v.; [and therefore] anomalous. (Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
